title: Banashak's drinking, gambling and born-again faith
summary: Banashak's life swung from drinking and gambling to born-again Christianity, with disillusionment, marital trouble and effects on A1.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: And you have to remember, Joe went through these major personal life changes, too, along the way. When he first started, you know, he was a straightforward guy. And then he got into drinking and gambling real bad. Mm-hmm. And then he straightened out to the enormous extent that a born-again Christian does. He became... He was a Roman Catholic, a devout one, incidentally. Mm-hmm. Come from Baltimore, you know.

Right. And he became a born-again Christian. Mm-hmm. And... Jeez, I hope nobody ever holds me to this in the wrong way. Those kinds of people have this enormous ability to rationalize things by the tenets of their faith. And Joe quit drinking, you know, quit gambling, got to where he was very straight-laced in his lifestyle. Right. You know? Yeah. And I think somewhere along the way, a couple of people he was involved with in that kind of disillusioned him, a pastor or somebody, whatever. But he never really gave it up. He remained, but he changed churches and stuff. And I think there was some pain in his personal life over it.

Because he really had subsumed into that religious mode. Mm-hmm. And he, I think, was kind of disillusioned with some personal, again, you know, people letting him down because he put... He invested faith in these certain people and they turned out to be less than perhaps he believed and that kind of stuff. And he had marital problems and stuff like that.
So all of this, of course, is affecting his business.

Yes. I'm assuming so. Yes. Well, when he got to really drinking and gambling bed, he would never admit it. But it was part of the problem, the latter-day problems of A1. You know, he was losing a fair amount of money at the track. And by going to the track instead of being at A1, he was losing in other ways. And we talked about it from time to time. I considered him a true friend, a real gentleman.
And, I don't know. He had some painful life experience because of it.
